column1: # Log signatures that suggest the gate could not RUN, as opposed to running and
# finding a defect.   scope <TAB> label <TAB> extended regular expression
# Matched case-insensitively. Lines starting with # are comments.
# Shared by engine/gate-report.py (the v0 log-heuristic adapter) and
# engine/gate_report.py (the v2 normalizer) through engine/infra_patterns.py.
# They used to disagree: the patterns lived only in the hyphenated module, which
# the v2 path never calls, so on v2 they were dead code and every gate that
# exited non-zero without an observation was reported as a product failure.
# SCOPE is what keeps fixing that from causing the opposite bug. The two callers
# have very different costs of being wrong:
#   strict     — used by BOTH paths. An infrastructure verdict on v2 becomes
#                inconclusive-infrastructure, which l1-drive maps to audit-infra,
#                which the decider parks UNCONDITIONALLY without consulting the
#                retry budget. So a false positive here kills a task that a retry
#                would have fixed. Only signatures that application code under
#                test cannot plausibly produce on its own belong in this tier.
#   heuristic  — v0 adapter only, where the classification merely annotates a
#                result. These fire on real application failures often enough
#                that promoting them would trade a budget-burn bug for a
#                task-death bug: a test opening a missing fixture prints "no such
#                file or directory"; a service test refusing a connection prints
#                ECONNREFUSED; an app writing somewhere it shouldn't prints
#                EACCES. All three are ordinary product defects.
strict
strict
strict
strict
column3: \bcommand not found\b|\bis not recognized as an internal or external command\b

column1: # TS2688 / a bare "cannot find module" with no adapter report. A worktree that is
# missing a nested node_modules cannot resolve the @types packages tsconfig asks
# for, and tsc reports it exactly like this. Without a dependency provision step, the
# auditor's disposable worktree never received the monorepo's nested dependency
# trees, so a gate that was green for the worker failed there and normalized to a
# product defect nobody could fix. A worker CAN write a genuinely broken import
# that looks the same — but only when the gate emitted no structured observation
# at all, which for a repo with a real gate adapter never happens.
strict
strict
column3: \bcannot find module\b|\bmodule not found\b|\bmissing dependency\b|\bmodulenotfounderror\b|\bcannot find package\b
